- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3+ in 3-day window), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to avoid mean-reversion lag.
- Model frequently overpredicts 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate from 10-day window onward with sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- Avoid forecasting price > 20% above recent 14-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.80) and confirmed over 3 consecutive days.
